blocks.title: Privacy partitions, built in series
blocks.lead: We design, tool and manufacture interior partitions for premium vehicles, and supply them to dealers and conversion shops as a kit that is ready to trim and fit.

blocks.title: An engineering company, not a tuning shop
body: We do not work on an individual car. We work on a car model: every project runs from 3D scanning of the interior through to production tooling, so the product can be built in series with repeatable geometry and repeatable quality.

Our clients are vehicle distributors, official dealerships and specialist conversion shops. They receive a kit ready for installation; trimming, fitting and final finishing are carried out by the partner, following our templates and instructions.

blocks.title: Two classes of solution
blocks.lead: The difference is not in the partition but in how much of the interior has to come apart to fit it. That decides which kind of partner can install the product.

items.title: Simple — 3 to 4 kits a year
items.text: Fitted without a wholesale rebuild of the interior. The partition carries a glass raise-and-lower mechanism, sometimes fixed glass, and optionally electric curtains. Factory monitors and factory multimedia are used. The work is within reach of a dealer workshop: we installed the Rolls-Royce partitions on the official dealer's premises, using the dealer's own technicians.

items.title: Complex — 30 to 40 kits a year
items.text: These require a rebuild of the interior. At minimum a new rear bench with a console goes in; usually the whole rear is rebuilt — headliner, side panels, multimedia, lighting. We supply a partition ready for installation, and the partner needs to be a company capable of serious vehicle conversion.

pages.title: Product
pages.title_tag: What a 7pro8 partition adds, and what it leaves alone
pages.description: A privacy partition turns the rear of a premium car into a separate working compartment — without cutting the body, disturbing the airbags or voiding the interior.

blocks.title: What the partition adds, and what it leaves alone
blocks.lead: A partition changes what the car is for. The engineering question that decides whether an owner will accept it is the second one: what does the conversion take away?

items.title: Privacy on demand
items.text: Electrochromic glass changes opacity at the touch of a button, the glass raises and lowers electrically, and the curtains are electrically operated. Privacy is there when it is wanted and out of the way when it is not.

items.title: Acoustic separation
items.text: A physical partition with the glass raised separates the rear from the front. Calls, meetings and documents stay in the rear, in the presence of a driver, a security detail or a hired chauffeur.

items.title: A rear that works as an office
items.text: Electrically operated folding seats, a console armrest, sliding boxes, a monitor up to 43 inches with electric lift, an intercom, a pass-through hatch, and auxiliary instruments — clock, speedometer, thermometer.

items.title: A level that is not on the factory price list
items.text: Among the models we work with, only the Rolls-Royce Phantom Extended has a factory partition — the Privacy Suite, from 2018, and only when ordering a new car. For Maybach, V-Class, Range Rover, Escalade and Sprinter no factory solution exists, including for cars already in service.

items.title: A change of vehicle category
items.text: The car moves from executive to chauffeur-driven: transport for company principals, diplomatic missions, VIP transfer and escorted travel. A different class of task, and a different price segment of service.

items.title: An interior that still looks factory
items.text: Trimming is carried out in materials from the vehicle manufacturer's own palette — leather, wood veneer, Alcantara. The interior stays whole rather than looking modified.

blocks.title: The objection every owner raises
body: Premium car owners do not ask whether the partition looks good. They ask whether the conversion will spoil the car — its safety systems, its diagnostics, its residual value.
Our answer is not a promise about the quality of the installer's work. It is six decisions built into the product itself, which hold whoever fits it.

image.alt: Mercedes-Maybach S-Class interior with the partition in place
image.caption: Mercedes-Maybach S-Class (X222) — the partition sits inside the factory architecture of the interior

items.title: Body structure
items.text: The partition is a self-supporting module that sits on factory and prepared mounting points. The body is neither cut nor welded; the geometry and stiffness of the vehicle are untouched.

items.title: Passive safety
items.text: Factory belts and pretensioners, side and curtain airbags and seat mountings stay in place and work to factory logic. The partition sits between the rows and does not enter their deployment zones.

items.title: Vehicle electronics
items.text: Connection is made through factory connectors. The partition's wiring runs on a separate loom with its own protection. Factory data buses are not reprogrammed, so vehicle diagnostics stay clean.

items.title: Rear climate zone
items.text: The geometry of the partition is developed around the factory airflow, so the rear climate zone continues to work as the manufacturer designed it.

items.title: Interface and multimedia
items.text: Wherever possible the factory monitors and factory multimedia are used. The owner keeps using the familiar interface of the car rather than a parallel system.

items.title: Reversibility
items.text: Removal takes one to three days and the car returns to factory configuration. This protects residual value and removes the question at resale or lease return.

blocks.title: In short
body: The car keeps everything the owner paid the manufacturer for, and gains a function the manufacturer does not offer. The conversion does not compete with factory engineering — it sits on top of it, and can be taken off again.

blocks.title: Which car do you need it for?
blocks.text: Nine models are documented in the portfolio, and a new one takes up to a year to develop.

blocks.title: One team, from the first sketch to the finished kit
blocks.lead: Design, engineering, tooling manufacture and production are all done in-house. A partner does not have to coordinate several subcontractors, and there is nowhere for responsibility to fall between them.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: The design is signed off before engineering begins, so the partner sees the result before money is committed to the project.

steps.title: Engineering
steps.text: Development and tooling are entirely ours — including joint projects where the partner produces part of the panels.

steps.title: Production
steps.text: The kit ships assembled and checked. What is left for the partner is trimming, fitting and connection.

blocks.title: Joint production, when that suits the partner better
body: A partner can take on exactly the share of production it is equipped for — from a complete turnkey kit down to a single structural frame with mechanisms. Development and tooling stay with us in every case.

On the Sprinter we supply the frame with the driver's side fully prepared for trimming, and the partner makes the composite panels of the VIP side. The same model runs on the Range Rover and on the Mercedes-Maybach.

pages.title: Manufacturing
pages.title_tag: Why tooling matters more than craftsmanship
pages.description: Composites, metal work and 3D printing in-house. Every 7pro8 partition is formed from production tooling, so gaps, joints and mounting points repeat from the first kit to the two-hundredth.

blocks.title: Why tooling matters more than craftsmanship
blocks.lead: A partition fitted by hand exists in a single copy: the next one will be different. Tooling is what turns a good result into a repeatable one.

body: We invest from €70,000 and up to a year of work to obtain the tooling for a model. After that, every unit repeats the master. Gaps, joints and mounting points are identical on the first kit and on the two-hundredth.
For a partner that means two things that show up directly in the workshop's costing: installation time can be planned, and there is no rework.

blocks.title: An engineering company, not a tuning shop
blocks.lead: 7pro8 produced its first interior partition in 2007. Since then we have developed more than 20 partition models for Mercedes-Benz, Mercedes-Maybach, Rolls-Royce, Range Rover and Cadillac, and delivered over 450 kits.

body: We do not work on an individual car — we work on a car model. Every project is a full cycle: from 3D scanning of the interior to the manufacture of production tooling that lets the product be built in series, with repeatable geometry and repeatable quality. That is what separates us from one-off customisation.

Our clients are vehicle distributors, official dealerships and specialist conversion shops. We supply them a kit ready for installation; trimming, fitting and final finishing are carried out by the partner, following our templates and instructions.
The company is based in Novi Sad, Serbia, and is led by Evgenii Abramov and Iliya Bolshakov.

DRAFT. A second paragraph on how he works. One or two concrete examples beat any amount of description.

blocks.title: The work, newest first
blocks.lead: Twelve projects across more than twenty years, in reverse order: the present at the top, the beginning at the bottom.

entries.title: Electric trike with a canopy
body: DRAFT. A personal project outside cars: frame, protective canopy and seating layout for two. Built entirely by hand, from the structure to final assembly.

images.alt: Trike with the canopy raised, in a field
images.caption: Canopy raised

entries.title: Interiors on the water
body: DRAFT. Work on boat and yacht interiors: the same problem as in a car, but different materials, different humidity and different rules. Projects from this period appeared in the trade press.

entries.title: Taxi roof sign
body: DRAFT. An illuminated roof sign for taxis: design, 3D model, tooling and series production. Small in size but complete in cycle — the same route from sketch to volume that the partitions would take ten years later.

images.alt: Taxi with the roof sign fitted
images.caption: Fitted to the car

entries.title: ZiL-4107 — state limousine interior
body: DRAFT. A complete rebuild of the interior of a Soviet state limousine. The project began as hand sketches — rear compartment layout, seating, trim — and ran through to a finished interior.

entries.title: Mercedes-Benz S-Class W221 — the first partition
body: DRAFT. The first partition, and where 7pro8 starts counting. The project ran through the full cycle that later became the standard: sketch, 3D model, engineering of the glass lift mechanism, tooling, finished product.
Everything the company builds in series today grew out of this job.

images.alt: Sketch of the interior with the partition
images.caption: Sketch

images.alt: CAD model of the partition frame
images.caption: Frame engineering

entries.title: Mercedes-Benz Vito — VIP interior
body: DRAFT. A van turned into a mobile office: individual seats, consoles, multimedia and an interior partition. An early example of exactly the kind of work the series business was later built on.

entries.title: Lamborghini Diablo VT
body: DRAFT. A full interior rebuild of a supercar: centre console, instrument area, audio system, leather and carbon trim. Work that demands exact fit in a cramped cabin with no flat surfaces at all.

entries.title: Chevrolet Corvette
body: DRAFT. The interior of a classic Corvette: a new centre console, trim and equipment. One of the run of projects that, in the early 2000s, turned Russian tuning into an industry.

entries.title: Hummer H1 — VIP interior
body: DRAFT. An off-roader turned into an executive interior: bench seat, veneer trim, ambient lighting, multimedia. Built for a private client.
THE CLIENT IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED HERE — see the note on this page.

entries.title: Lincoln Reincarnation
body: DRAFT. The most visible project of the early period: a car with a completely rebuilt body and interior, shown at exhibitions and covered by the press. The project name stayed attached to the studio for years.

images.alt: The car from the rear, lights on
images.caption: Rear lighting

entries.title: Workshop, team, first volumes
body: DRAFT. The period when a workshop became a company with production of its own: design, model shop, metalwork, upholstery, veneer, electronics — all under one roof.

images.alt: The studio team by a car
images.caption: The team

entries.title: Before the studio: a garage, racing, the press
body: DRAFT. The very beginning: hands-on work in an unheated garage, home-built projects out of whatever was to hand, circuit racing and the first contacts in the motoring press. This is where it all came from.
